description.value: The Fernie Museum, operated by the Fernie & District Historical Society, occupies two floors in Historic Downtown Fernie and traces 140 years of Elk Valley history through its permanent 'This Is Our Fernie' exhibit and rotating second-floor gallery. An archives and collections centre supports research visits, and summer walking tours cover colourful local history including the 1908 Great Fire and Prohibition-era rum-running. Admission is by donation, making it an accessible and rewarding cultural stop for cyclists touring the Kootenays.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is fully available and corroborates all OSM contact fields (phone, address, website). The visiting page explicitly states 'Barrier free public washrooms' and 'Free public WiFi,' making those amenities positively confirmed. No bike rack, water refill station, or any bike-specific infrastructure is mentioned anywhere on the site; the parking references describe vehicle parking on 2nd Ave, 5th St, and behind the museum only.
concerns: OSM tag 'fee: yes' conflicts with website which states 'Admission is by donation' — website is the authoritative source.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active, publicly accessible local history museum in Historic Downtown Fernie with confirmed barrier-free washrooms and free WiFi; a worthwhile cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Kootenays.

blurb: Elk Valley history museum in downtown Fernie; summer walking tours of the 1908 Great Fire story.
